rejected.title: The Declaration of Independence
card: On 4 July 1776, the Continental Congress, a meeting of delegates from the colonies, approved the Declaration of Independence. It announced that the thirteen colonies were no longer part of the British Empire.
Thomas Jefferson was the main author. The document says people have natural rights, and that governments get their power from the consent of the governed.
It lists many grievances, or complaints, against King George III. These include keeping armies in the colonies in peacetime and taxing the colonists without their consent.
The Declaration argues that when a government abuses its power, the people may change it. Blaming the king gave the colonists a reason for breaking away.
rejected.remember: The Declaration announced independence and justified it by blaming the king for abuses.

a.q: Why did the Declaration of Independence list grievances against the king?
opts: To justify breaking away from British rule
To ask Parliament to repeal the colonial taxes
To set out the laws of the new government
To list the rights of each of the colonies
a.why: The grievances were the reasons given for independence. They argued that the king had abused his power, so the colonists could change their government. It was not a request to Parliament, because the document already declared the colonies independent.
a.clue: Think about what the colonists needed to show the world.

b.q: A student says the Declaration of Independence was written to win the war against Britain. Which reply is best?
opts: It announced independence and gave reasons, not a war win
It ended the fighting, because Britain accepted it in 1776
It created the new government and set out its laws
It was a plan for how the colonists would raise an army
b.why: The Declaration stated that the colonies were independent and gave reasons. It did not end the fighting or set up a government. The tempting option is the one saying Britain accepted it, but Britain rejected the claim and the war continued.
b.clue: Ask what a statement of reasons can and cannot do on a battlefield.

version.title: The Declaration of Independence
card: On 4 July 1776 the Continental Congress, made up of delegates from the thirteen colonies, adopted the Declaration of Independence. It stated that the colonies were now free and independent states.
Drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson, it opens with ideas of rights and consent. It then argues that a people may break from a government that abuses its power.
Most of the document is a list of grievances, or complaints, against King George III, such as keeping soldiers in the colonies in peacetime and taxing colonists without their consent.
The grievances blamed the king, presenting the break as a response to tyranny. The Declaration did not end the war: fighting went on until 1781, and Britain recognised independence in 1783.
version.remember: The Declaration announced the break and used a list of the king's wrongs to justify it.

a.q: What was the main purpose of the long list of grievances in the Declaration?
opts: To justify breaking away from British rule
To ask Parliament to repeal the colonial taxes
To set out the laws of the new United States
To offer peace terms the king could accept
a.why: The grievances were the reasons for independence: they argued the king had abused his power, so the colonists were right to break away. It was not a request for repeal, because the document already declared the colonies independent.
a.clue: Think about what the colonists needed to show the world.

b.q: A student says the Declaration of Independence won the colonies their freedom in 1776. Which reply best corrects the student?
opts: It declared independence, but war decided it later
It ended the war, as Britain accepted it at once
It was a petition asking the king for more rights
It was signed by Britain as a peace treaty in 1776
b.why: The Declaration stated that the colonies were independent and gave reasons, but Britain did not accept it. Fighting went on until 1781, and Britain recognised independence only in 1783.

a.best: To justify breaking away from British rule

b.best: It declared independence, but war decided it later

problems.detail: "Fighting went on until 1781" suggests all fighting stopped in 1781. The last major battle, Yorktown, was in 1781, but smaller fighting on land and at sea went on into 1782 and 1783. Saying "major fighting ended at Yorktown in 1781" would be accurate. The why for b repeats the same wording.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one right answer. One small fact to tighten: the card says fighting went on until 1781, when only major fighting ended then (Yorktown), and smaller fighting continued until the 1783 peace.
